my_sentences.en: Can I ask you something?
my_sentences.ko: 뭐 하나 물어봐도 돼?
→ 상대방에게 질문하기 전에 자연스럽게 허락을 구하는 표현이야.

my_sentences.en: Can I ask you something? Why did you quit your job?
my_sentences.ko: 뭐 하나 물어봐도 돼? 왜 회사 그만뒀어?

my_sentences.en: Can I ask you something? Are you seeing anyone?
my_sentences.ko: 뭐 하나 물어봐도 돼? 너 만나는 사람 있어?

my_sentences.en: Can I ask you something about your job?
my_sentences.ko: 네 일에 대해서 뭐 하나 물어봐도 돼?

my_sentences.en: Can I ask you something personal?
my_sentences.ko: 개인적인 거 하나 물어봐도 돼?

my_sentences.en: ② absolutely necessary
my_sentences.ko: 완전히 필요한, 꼭 필요한
→ necessary만 써도 "필요한"이라는 뜻이지만,
absolutely necessary는 "정말 반드시 필요한"이라는 강한 느낌이야.

my_sentences.en: Do you think this is absolutely necessary?
my_sentences.ko: 이게 정말 꼭 필요하다고 생각해?

my_sentences.en: Is it absolutely necessary to go there?
my_sentences.ko: 거기 꼭 가야 해?

my_sentences.en: I don't think it's absolutely necessary.
my_sentences.ko: 난 그게 꼭 필요하다고 생각하지 않아.

my_sentences.en: It's absolutely necessary if you want to succeed.
my_sentences.ko: 성공하고 싶다면 그건 정말 꼭 필요해.

my_sentences.en: Is it absolutely necessary to finish this today?
my_sentences.ko: 이거 오늘 꼭 끝내야 해?
Is it absolutely necessary to + 동사?
~하는 게 정말 꼭 필요한가?
It just seems like + 문장 : 그냥 ~인 것 같아서

my_sentences.en: It just seems like a lot of people are successful these days.
my_sentences.ko: 요즘 성공한 사람들이 많은 것 같

my_sentences.en: It just seems like everyone is busy these days.
my_sentences.ko: 요즘 그냥 다들 바쁜 것 같아.

my_sentences.en: It just seems like he's avoiding me.
my_sentences.ko: 그냥 걔가 나를 피하는 것 같아.

my_sentences.en: It just seems like things are getting more expensive.
my_sentences.ko: 그냥 물가가 점점 비싸지는 것 같아.

my_sentences.en: It just seems like nobody cares anymore.
my_sentences.ko: 그냥 이제 아무도 신경 안 쓰는 것 같아.

my_sentences.en: It just seems like a good opportunity.
my_sentences.ko: 그냥 좋은 기회인 것 같아.

my_sentences.en: 4.  have no problems ~ing
my_sentences.ko: ~하는 데 아무 문제가 없다

my_sentences.en: have no problems making a living
my_sentences.ko: 먹고사는 데 아무 문제가 없다

my_sentences.en: I have no problems making a living.
my_sentences.ko: 난 먹고사는 데 아무 문제 없어.

my_sentences.en: He has no problems making friends.
my_sentences.ko: 걔는 친구 사귀는 데 아무 문제가 없어.

my_sentences.en: She has no problems finding a job.
my_sentences.ko: 그녀는 일자리를 구하는 데 아무 문제가 없어.

my_sentences.en: They have no problems paying their bills.
my_sentences.ko: 그들은 생활비를 내는 데 아무 문제가 없어.

my_sentences.en: I don't think you'll have any problems adjusting.
my_sentences.ko: 네가 적응하는 데 별문제 없을 것 같아.

my_sentences.en: I've been thinking a lot about ~ lately
my_sentences.ko: 최근에 ~에 대해 많이 고민하고 있어
→ 현재까지 이어지고 있는 고민/생각을 말할 때 아주 유용해.

my_sentences.en: I've been thinking a lot about my future lately.
my_sentences.ko: 최근에 미래에 대해 많이 고민하고 있어.

my_sentences.en: I've been thinking a lot about my career lately.
my_sentences.ko: 최근에 진로에 대해 많이 고민하고 있어.

my_sentences.en: I've been thinking a lot about moving lately.
my_sentences.ko: 최근에 이사하는 걸 많이 생각하고 있어.

my_sentences.en: I've been thinking a lot about quitting my job lately.
my_sentences.ko: 최근에 회사를 그만두는 걸 많이 고민하고 있어.

my_sentences.en: I've been thinking a lot about what I want to do with my life lately.
my_sentences.ko: 최근에 내가 앞으로 뭘 하고 살고 싶은지 많이 생각하고 있어.

my_sentences.en: I've been thinking a lot about saving money lately.
my_sentences.ko: 최근에 돈을 저축하는 것에 대해 많이 생각하고 있어.

my_sentences.en: 6.  Are you saying you want to ~?
my_sentences.ko: 너 ~하겠다는 거야?
→ 상대방의 말을 듣고 "그러니까 네 말은 ~하겠다는 거야?"라고 되묻는 표현.

my_sentences.en: Are you saying you want to quit your job?
my_sentences.ko: 너 그래서 회사 그만두겠다는 거야?

my_sentences.en: Are you saying you want to move out?
my_sentences.ko: 너 독립하겠다는 거야?

my_sentences.en: Are you saying you don't trust me?
my_sentences.ko: 너 나를 못 믿겠다는 거야?

my_sentences.en: Are you saying you want to break up with me?
my_sentences.ko: 너 나랑 헤어지겠다는 거야?

my_sentences.en: Are you saying you don't want to go?
my_sentences.ko: 너 안 가겠다는 거야?

my_sentences.en: I'm just saying.
my_sentences.ko: 그냥 그렇다는 거야 / 그냥 내 말은 그렇다는 거야.

my_sentences.en: I'm not criticizing you. I'm just saying.
my_sentences.ko: 너 비난하는 거 아니야. 그냥 그렇다는 거야.
Please don't tell me + 문장 : 설마 ~인 건 아니지?
→ 이건 상대방이 안 좋은 소식을 말할 것 같을 때 쓰는 아주 회화적인 표현이야.

my_sentences.en: Please don't tell me you quit your job.
my_sentences.ko: 설마 너 회사 그만둔 건 아니지?

my_sentences.en: Please don't tell me you forgot again.
my_sentences.ko: 설마 또 잊어버린 건 아니지?

my_sentences.en: Please don't tell me you lost your phone.
my_sentences.ko: 설마 핸드폰 잃어버린 건 아니지?

my_sentences.en: Please don't tell me you spent all the money.
my_sentences.ko: 설마 돈을 다 써버린 건 아니지?

my_sentences.en: Please don't tell me you're quitting.
my_sentences.ko: 설마 그만두는 건 아니지?

my_sentences.en: Please don't tell me we're late.
my_sentences.ko: 설마 우리 늦은 건 아니지?
